title: Big Outdoor Loose Parts
strapline: Crates, tyres, planks and cable reels — heavy, movable, buildable stuff for whole-body, big-idea construction.
intent: Children build on a grand scale, moving, lifting and balancing materials big enough to climb on and inside.
Children solve real engineering and physics problems — will the plank balance, will the den stay up, will the ramp roll?
Children build core strength, coordination and confidence through genuine heavy work.
Children negotiate, plan and cooperate — big builds need more than one pair of hands.
Children assess and manage risk, judging what is safe and steady for themselves.
implementation: Provide crates, tyres, planks, cable reels, guttering, pallets and tubes, stored where children can fetch them.
Stand back and let the build be the children's — offer a hand to lift, not a design to copy.
Coach the heavy-work talk — 'bend your knees, ask a friend, is it steady?' — and let bodies do the learning.
Support risk assessment through questions rather than bans: 'how could you test if that's safe to stand on?'
Feed in the physics and maths — balance, ramps, how many crates make it tall enough, will it hold your weight?
Give big builds a purpose and a story — a pirate ship, a bus, a den, a rushing marble ramp.
Let unfinished builds stay overnight where you can, so a project can grow across days.
key_questions: How could you make that steady enough to stand on?
Do you need a friend to lift that with you?
How can we test whether the bridge will hold your weight?
How many crates until the tower is as tall as you?
Which way should the plank go to make the ramp roll faster?

impact.text: Children build, balance and construct on a big scale, solving real engineering problems.
Children move, lift and carry heavy materials, building core strength and coordination.
Children assess and manage risk, judging for themselves what is safe and steady.
Children negotiate, plan and cooperate on builds too big for one child.
Children explore balance, ramps and forces and test their ideas by building.
Children count crates and compare heights and lengths as they build.
Children persist with a wobbly build until it holds, and feel the win.

enhancements: Crates, tyres, planks, pallets, cable reels and guttering in a fetchable store.
Guttering and balls for building rolling ramps and runs.
Fabric, pegs and clips for turning a frame into a den or a boat.
Rope and pulleys for hauling materials up and along.
Wheelbarrows and trolleys for moving the heavy parts.
A build-of-the-week photo wall to inspire and record.
Hard hats and clipboards for the site engineers.

playing_exploring: Children take real physical risks and test what their bodies and materials can do.
The same crates become a ship, a bus and a tower across a single week.
active_learning: Big builds demand persistence — lift, balance, rebuild, try again.
Children set ambitious goals and stick with them across days.
creating_thinking: Children plan, test and adapt their structures, learning from every collapse.
They solve balance, height and strength problems with their own experiments.
